greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. Grab a coffee, there's plenty happening in AI and across Victoria today.

lead.headline: Anthropic files for a Nasdaq IPO under the ticker 'ANT'
lead.summary: Anthropic filed its S-1 with the US securities regulator on October 26, reporting $16.3 billion in first-half revenue. The filing seeks a listing of Class A shares on Nasdaq.

stories.headline: Shaped laser light flips magnetic memory states without a magnetic field
stories.summary: Published in Nature Communications, UC San Diego researchers used shaped ultrafast laser pulses to switch magnetic domains in a nine-layer platinum-cobalt structure, a step toward much faster memory. It is drawing press attention for the claim of roughly 1,000x faster memory, though chip integration remains a challenge.

stories.headline: Five silicon spin qubits run at once with about 99.9% fidelity
stories.summary: In Nature Physics, RIKEN-led researchers operated five qubits sharing one microwave line simultaneously, correcting the AC Stark shift error with a pair-based calibration. It addresses a key scaling obstacle for quantum computers and is being widely covered.

stories.headline: ReviewScore: spotting flawed premises in AI-conference peer reviews
stories.summary: Presented in Findings of EMNLP 2026, the paper estimates that about 15% of review weaknesses and 26% of questions at AI conferences rest on mistaken premises, and tests LLMs at flagging them. Agreement with human experts was only moderate, so full automation is still hard.

stories.headline: Banks and Blackstone line up $63B to lease Broadcom chips to Anthropic
stories.summary: Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley committed $63 billion to a vehicle that will buy Broadcom accelerators and lease them to Anthropic, with deliveries from 2027.

stories.headline: Cloudflare says a cache bug leaked 155 AI responses between users
stories.summary: A tenant-isolation flaw in Cloudflare's serving stack returned other users' prompt data between August 27 and September 9. The company found no evidence of deliberate exploitation.

stories.headline: Boston Dynamics staff push back on robot dog sale to ICE
stories.summary: More than 300 employees petitioned executives to halt a $1.3 million contract with the US Department of Homeland Security. Management says it will proceed and that the robots won't be weaponised.

stories.headline: Labor proposes charging abusive patients for ambulance care
stories.summary: The election policy is welcomed by health workers, but advocates warn vulnerable people could be left without vital services.

stories.headline: Thomas Sewell pleads guilty over Camp Sovereignty violence
stories.summary: The neo-Nazi leader and three other men admitted charges linked to an alleged attack at Melbourne's Camp Sovereignty last year.

stories.headline: Erin Patterson's appeal decision due on Friday
stories.summary: Victoria's Court of Appeal will rule on Friday and could order a retrial or acquit her entirely if the appeal succeeds.

stories.headline: $180m federal funding for a controversial rare earths mine in western Victoria
stories.summary: Government backing for the Donald mineral sands project has drawn opposition from farmers and locals.

stories.headline: Exit polls suggest a rebuke of Netanyahu but no clear winner in Israel's election
stories.summary: Early exit polls point to a setback for Netanyahu, though neither his bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's appears to hold a clear majority.

stories.headline: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide after the Gaza truce
stories.summary: A UN commission of inquiry concluded that the alleged genocide against Palestinians continued after the ceasefire took hold.

thought: The best way to predict the future is to invent it. — Alan Kay
